content: Do we have for finitely generated field extension K/k, any algebraic independent set over k must be finite? I loogled Algebra.EssFiniteType and AlgebraicIndependent/IsTranscendenceBasis but didn't find useful stuffs.

Don't know if we have it but the way to do it is to prove the matroidy-like lemmas for transcendence bases -- any K-algebraically independent elements of L can be extended to a transcendence basis and any collection of elements such that L/(K-extension generated by them) is algebraic has a subset which is a transcendence basis
We already have this, but the problem is I am needing this for any transcendental basis.
Oh yeah you also need that any two transcendence bases have the same cardinality and that should be everything
My problem is in finitely generated separably generated extension, I we only know there is a transcendental basis such that the extension above is separable, I want to know something about the basis.
